## Decision and current state

Oxfmt 0.74.0 and Oxlint 1.89.0 are the canonical repository tools. Run
`bun format` and `bun lint` for checks, or `bun ff` for safe lint fixes followed
by formatting. CI runs `oxfmt --check .` and
`oxlint --deny-warnings --threads 2 .`. Editor integrations use the local tools. Markdown, MDX and YAML remain outside
Oxfmt formatting; generated byte-freshness artifacts retain their owning generators.
CSS overrides use double quotes to retain stylesheet and source-registration contracts;
JavaScript and TypeScript retain single quotes.
Generated route trees, bridge registries, generated API clients, vendored skill
catalogs and paused runtimes remain outside traversal. The Security Checks workflow
retains its reviewed bytes and is excluded from formatting; its byte seal remains
unchanged. Wrangler usage digests require an explicit formatting-only PR admission.

Oxc formatting is independent of Cloudflare runtime adoption. Vite+ consolidates
tooling; it does not translate routes, server components or server actions.
Lint parity is approximate: the configuration retains the correctness preset with
explicit exclusions for React Compiler diagnostics, dependency analysis and rules
whose semantics exceed the repository baseline. The explicit `react/no-danger` error preserves the unsafe-HTML guard. Sanitized
HTML exceptions are individual line suppressions tied to a reviewed sanitizer.
Type checks remain required.
CSS lint rules and import organization do not have automatic parity; review these
separately. The pinned configuration is the executable rule inventory.

### Formatting conflicts in open pull requests

Manually merge main into the PR branch first. From the repository root, run
`node scripts/resolve-format-conflicts.js --main origin/main` for a dry run, then
repeat with `--apply`. The selected ref must equal `MERGE_HEAD`. The helper only
considers unmerged JS/TS files changed on the PR and proves that normalized base
and incoming-main blobs match using the pinned formatter. It retains the PR blob
and formats it. Real semantic changes, manual conflict edits, unsupported paths,
symlinks, binary content and add/delete/rename conflicts are refused before writes.
Targets are opened with no-follow flags before inspecting their descriptor
metadata; no pathname precheck authorizes access. Checked regular-file descriptors
retain device/inode identity for reads and writes. Nonblocking open rejects
non-regular targets without waiting on FIFO peers. Parent containment and identity are rechecked; path replacement refuses
without following the replacement. The helper is not a crash-atomic multi-file writer.
Only ordinary merge conflict markers are supported; diff3/zdiff3 conflicts need
manual resolution. Files with no conflicts are left alone. No index update,
commit, merge or push occurs. Inspect the diff and stage resolutions manually.
Regression coverage: `node --test scripts/resolve-format-conflicts.test.js`.

Lettin and Parley already have Next.js/OpenNext Worker deployments. Their next
architecture milestone is the same per-app TanStack Start + Void + Vite+ Worker
runtime as the other web apps, reaching `next/*` only through
`@tuturuuu/start-bridge` and preserving existing contracts. See the
[native Start migration runbook](/build/devops/native-start-migration). The
retired `apps/tanstack-web` is not revived.

## Platform-wide target and per-operation receipts

The ultimate target is **every active application using Vite+, hosted on
Cloudflare, with Oxc linting/formatting**. Work proceeds incrementally alongside
the product backlog; the initial Worker inventory below is the first wave, not a
limit on the program. Retained paused applications remain excluded until resumed.
Mobile continues to use its native Flutter toolchain; shared services and web
surfaces follow the platform target without implying a rewrite of native UI.

The **cf/Void Wrangler-exit lane** drains a single checked-in operation queue in
`scripts/ci/fixtures/cf-toolchain-receipts.json`. Each operation records isolated
rehearsal evidence, the implementation path, production template (when
applicable), allowlist deltas and Wrangler gaps that stay until their explicit
removal conditions pass. `node scripts/ci/cf-toolchain-receipts.mjs` validates the
queue; `node --test scripts/ci/cf-toolchain-receipts.test.mjs` proves referenced
parity fixtures exist. A `switched` receipt marks the authoritative toolchain for
that operation; `qualified` keeps Wrangler publication or CLI until the next gate
closes; `gap` names the owner and remaining conditions only.

Keep per-app ownership, prerequisites and exact-head receipts in the private
request backlog and coordination board. Record per-operation receipts and explicit
removal conditions for each Wrangler/cf operation. Separate implemented,
CI-verified, runtime-accepted and production-delivered states. A merge does not
establish hosting cutover. Capture new Worker/app scope and compatibility
findings before dispatching the next operation; avoid competing migration and
product owners in the same files.

## Complete Worker migration scope

The migration includes every active Worker-backed app/service, not only Lettin
and Parley. Framework replacement applies to Next/OpenNext web apps; native
Workers retain their fetch/email/scheduled/RPC entrypoints while adopting Vite+
and Oxc tooling. A backend service does not need React or a router to qualify.

| Active surface | Current boundary | Migration acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Meet | Next/OpenNext web Worker and shared Meet services | Vite-native web routes; preserve meeting/session APIs, AI entrypoints, media and Durable Object classes |
| Parley | Next/OpenNext web Worker | Vite-native studio and participant routes; preserve private reviews, snapshots and Meet bindings |
| Lettin | Next/OpenNext web Worker with D1/R2 | Vite-native routes; preserve publication, ownership, D1 session and R2 contracts |
| Colab | Vite React assets plus native Worker | Adopt Vite+ without changing auth, sponsorship, room Durable Objects or SPA routing |
| Meet realtime | Native Worker and Durable Objects | Adopt shared tooling; preserve signalling, TURN/SFU contracts and realtime health checks |
| Chat realtime | cf + Void Worker with hibernating inbox and conversation Durable Objects | Bound fanout to two rooms per publish, deduplicate within the replay window, and verify the Worker stop secret and Web URL fence. See the [Chat realtime runbook](/build/devops/chat-realtime-runbook). |
| Coordination | Native Worker service | Preserve coordination protocol, authentication, object identity and storage |
| Mobile issue discovery | Cron Control processor, activation held | One query and at most one publish per admitted slot, a seven-day lease, and a durable stop fence. See the [Crashlytics runbook](/build/devops/mobile-store-deployment#crashlytics-discovery-on-cron-control) for operation limits and stop verification. |
| Ops Hub | New native Worker and per-user SQLite DO; publication held | Strict signed ingress, bounded storage/maintenance, durable stop fence; the operations runbook is internal |
| Devbox control | Native Worker service | Preserve control authentication, lease/state transitions and deployment identity |
| Cron control | Scheduled/native Worker | Preserve scheduler ownership, deduplication, recovery RPC and authenticated forwarding |
| Deploy coordinator | New native Worker and per-environment SQLite DO; publication held | No alarms, queues or outbound calls; catalog-bounded objects, durable daily call budget and environment stop fence. See the [deployment coordinator](/build/devops/deployment-coordinator) |
| Memory | Native Worker and cache-disabled Hyperdrive to the dedicated memory database; publication held | Per-caller durable stop epoch and finite admission budget, bounded requests and SQL, no schedules, retries or Worker-generated embeddings. See [AI Memory Service](/platform/ai/memory-service#worker-schema-and-stop-controls). |
| Vault witness | New cf + Void Worker with per-vault and per-user SQLite DOs; publication held for a dedicated account | No alarms, queues or outbound calls; durable per-minute and daily call budgets per object, storage caps, 256 KiB bodies and the `WITNESS_STOPPED` stop secret. See the [Secrets vault witness](/platform/architecture/secrets-vault-witness) |
| Mail email routing | Native email Worker within Mail | Preserve MIME ingestion, R2 permissions and the owning Mail webhook contract. Workers Logs are bounded to one invocation log per delivery attempt, with a script-settings stop that needs no build. See the [cost envelope and stop](/platform/applications/mail#email-routing-worker-logs). |

This inventory follows active checked-in Wrangler configurations. Existing
`apps/backend` and `apps/tanstack-web` Wrangler files are retained paused artifacts,
not migration targets. New active Worker configurations must join the inventory.
Deployment existence and canonical health still require live evidence.

Begin with the portable session core and the already Vite-native Colab toolchain,
then use the same verified conventions for native service workers. Meet, Parley
and Lettin require the shared framework-adapter work before full web replacement.
Each app retains its own exact-commit test/type/lint/build and Worker acceptance
receipts; one green app cannot establish another app's readiness.

## cf CLI adoption alongside Vite+

Prefer Cloudflare's **cf CLI** over Wrangler as each operation proves compatible.
The per-operation verdicts, native Worker template, guard and cutover checklist
live in [cf CLI and Void over Wrangler](/build/development-tools/cf-cli-wrangler-parity).
This is a phased tooling decision, separate from framework migration and production
promotion. Existing Wrangler commands/configurations remain authoritative until
that scope passes its replacement gates.

[Cloudflare's launch announcement](https://blog.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-cf-cli-launch/)
introduces cf in open beta, with JSON output and a generated API command surface.
Vite-built Workers can migrate to typed `cloudflare.config.ts`; configuration uses
Vite modes, whose semantics differ from Wrangler environments. cf still delegates
some development/deployment paths to Wrangler. Recheck upstream support before
implementing a scope; the announcement is not evidence of repository compatibility.

1. **Read-only discovery first.** Pin a reviewed cf version through the owning
   workspace's package manager. Verify help/schema, authentication and selected
   account independently; existing Wrangler login does not establish cf access.
   Exercise bounded inventory/observability queries and record supported command
   mappings. Filter JSON to required fields and keep raw logs/credentials private.
2. **Pilot a Vite-native Worker.** Coordination or Colab is a candidate after its
   Vite+ artifact gates pass. Review migration output in an isolated worktree;
   do not run a repository-wide migrator. Verify compatibility with the pinned
   Vite+ core, Cloudflare plugin and test runner before adopting typed configuration.
3. **Prove configuration and artifact parity.** Compare resolved settings for
   every used mode: account/name, routes/domains, compatibility date/flags, assets,
   service bindings, Durable Object names/classes/migrations, storage identifiers,
   triggers, secrets and observability. Preserve resource identity; never infer
   that a similarly named mode selects the same deployed environment. Select one
   authoritative configuration per scope, with an explicit fallback procedure.
4. **Replace operations separately.** Map local development, type generation,
   tests, CI bundling, validation upload, tail, version inspection, deployment and
   rollback individually. Unsupported or unverified operations retain Wrangler.
   CI must exercise the final emitted artifact and preserve exact-SHA and target
   identity checks; a CLI rename or dry run alone cannot establish runtime health.
5. **Roll out per owner.** Update scripts, workflow permissions, runbooks and skill
   references together after focused tests and exact-commit CI pass. Production
   commands change only with separately authorized promotion, bounded scope and
   verified rollback. Keep paused runtimes excluded.

### Discovery runtime and authentication

Use Node.js 22.18 or later to execute cf. Installing a dependency with Bun does
not mean the CLI should run on Bun: Cloudflare documents that commands loading
`cloudflare.config.ts` fail on the Bun runtime. Verify the executor separately
from the package manager. See [installation and authentication](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cf/get-started/).

For capability discovery before project adoption, run a reviewed, exact cf version
through `npm exec --yes --package=cf@<reviewed-version> -- cf --help` from a private
scratch directory outside app configuration and `.env` ancestry. This avoids a
global install or repository dependency change. Use an anonymous `cf cli search`
query describing the operation, then inspect that command's help/schema. Discovery
proves command availability, not authenticated operation or Worker artifact parity.

Parse `cf auth whoami` JSON and require `authenticated === true`; exit status zero
alone does not establish authentication. An unauthenticated result can return
`authenticated: false` and an error with a successful process exit. Preserve that
failure instead of proceeding to API calls. cf uses separate credentials from
Wrangler; do not copy credential files or assume a prior Wrangler login applies.

API commands can remember selected accounts in project-local cache files. Use
explicit target identity and isolate discovery before touching app worktrees;
review any resulting local files. Neither command discovery nor `--dry-run`
authorizes migration, configuration mutation, resource creation or deployment.

Cron Control, Devbox Control and Coordination pin `cf@1.0.0-beta.20` and use
`cloudflare.config.ts`, `vp dev` and `cf workers types`. Their existing per-service
CI checks qualify configuration and emitted output; this does not qualify legacy
Void or OpenNext configuration consumers. See the operation matrix for retained
publication gaps. The package pin requires Node `^22.23 || ^24.22 || ^26.12`;
the older Node 22.18 discovery minimum does not satisfy that package's engines.

Do not replace `wrangler types --config <emitted-config>` with a bare cf command:
type generation must read the same Worker identity and preserve the declarations
consumed by the app. Retain legacy local dev, D1 migration and tail commands until
their exact configuration, persistence and output contracts pass independently.
Calendar is the first emitted-config type-generation profile: its existing
validator admits only ASSETS, and the adapter runs the pinned cf CLI on a
supported Node executor. CI compares exact binding keys/requiredness/types against
the existing producer, verifies unchanged artifact bytes and retains a receipt.
Its self-contained declaration does not require shipping a generated config.
Other resource and framework profiles still require separate qualification.
Calendar's build-output comparison copies sealed ESM/assets into the cf format
and verifies the same bytes after restore. It retains the publisher because
secondary upload-module names and asset/runtime semantics need separate proof.

Track CLI capability gaps independently from app migration so an unsupported
operation does not block portable libraries or Oxc adoption.

## Qualify dependency resolution

Reconcile workspace requests with Bun's generated lockfile using the repository's
pinned Bun version. A manifest-only update can leave frozen installation blocked
before any type checking runs. Keep lifecycle scripts disabled during local
dependency inspection; require the normal exact-commit CI installation and builds.

Review effective tool dependencies as well as changed lock rows. Oxlint and Oxfmt
have optional Vite+ peers, so a Vite+ update can change their selected peer without
changing either tool's own row. Static scoped placements and a successful frozen
lockfile check do not prove the installer uses those placements. Resolve packages
from each owning app and tool after installation, record intentional peer changes,
and retain CI and emitted-runtime gates for the affected apps.

## Use the tooling foundation

From the repository root, pass **explicit files you own**:

```bash
bun oxc:lint scripts/oxc.js scripts/oxc.test.js
bun oxc:format scripts/oxc.js scripts/oxc.test.js
bun oxc:write scripts/oxc.js
node --test scripts/oxc.test.js
```

Lint fails on warnings/errors. Format checks do not write; `oxc:write` explicitly
applies formatting. The wrapper rejects empty selections, flags, globs, directories,
symlinks resolving outside the permitted source, build/dependency trees and paused
runtimes. Installed tools run with two threads, without Turbo or builds. Tests cover
scope rejection, debugger linting, read-only formatting and idempotence.

The baseline uses correctness rules with explicit exclusions, TypeScript/React/
accessibility plugins, and two-space, 80-column, single-quote, semicolon, LF,
ES5-trailing-comma formatting. This is **not Oxc rule parity**. Manifest sorting
is disabled; import and Tailwind sorting are not enabled.

## Rule parity follow-up

The root configuration lists every disabled rule. React Compiler rules and
`react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` need a separate behavioral adoption. Accessibility
rules need component-aware parity with existing intentional exceptions. Unused
variable and expression checks need matching TypeScript/test semantics. Arithmetic
and control-regex rules need fixture review before enabling. Next.js domain rules,
CSS linting, import organization and Tailwind sorting require dedicated parity
coverage; format success alone does not establish it. Keep type, accessibility,
security and runtime validation independent.

## First-party portability contract

Maintain domain rules and application services as ordinary TypeScript modules.
Reusable React components may depend on React and framework-independent UI
primitives; they receive navigation, translated labels and data through typed
props or a small explicitly scoped provider. React Server Components are an
optional adapter surface, never a prerequisite for consuming the domain package.

| Layer | Owns | Avoids |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Domain | Pure decisions, validation, immutable snapshots, permission predicates | Framework imports, request globals, storage drivers |
| Service | Workflows with injected actor, clock, repositories and capabilities | Reading ambient cookies/env or assuming trusted clients |
| Portable React UI | Semantic tokens, presentation, interaction state, accessibility | Next/router/translation hooks and server-only imports |
| Framework adapter | Route loaders/actions, HTTP mapping, navigation, localization, request credentials | Duplicating domain rules or bypassing policy |
| Runtime adapter | D1/R2/Supabase clients, Worker bindings and scheduling | Leaking credentials or runtime-specific types into portable exports |

Prefer existing first-party packages and narrow public subpath exports over a new
universal framework wrapper. Keep Next-specific compatibility entrypoints stable
while adding portable ones. Do not call an entire package framework-agnostic just
because one file is pure: consumers must resolve its entrypoint without transitively
loading Next/OpenNext or Cloudflare. Validate import graphs and consumer builds in
CI. Runtime-specific optional adapters must have explicit entrypoints/dependencies.

Use standard `Request`, `Response`, `Headers`, URLs and `AbortSignal` at HTTP
boundaries where appropriate. Pass request context per invocation; never store
actors or bindings in process-wide mutable state. Inject verified identity rather
than accepting browser-provided user IDs as authority. Preserve audience, expiry,
MFA, consent, membership and revocation checks in reusable policy services.

Current seams include Lettin's Actor/Store context and SQL permission fences,
with bindings/identity/HTTP as framework adapters. Parley/Meet domain contracts can
remain shared while routes, session lookup and meeting UI adapters are extracted.
A package can support Next.js, TanStack Start or other React hosts by implementing
these small adapters; support for every framework is a goal requiring consumer
verification, not an automatic guarantee.

## Vite-native Worker acceptance gates

Compare emitted compatibility flags against each service’s source configuration;
Devbox Control currently has no flags, so its verifier must not require
`nodejs_compat` simply because another Worker uses it.

| Boundary | Required preservation and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Routes | Public/private/API inventory, bilingual paths, redirects/rewrites, metadata, noindex and deep links |
| Identity | Satellite app-session audience/expiry, allowlists, MFA, workspace membership, owner consent and actor attribution |
| API | Existing internal-api contracts and TanStack Query; injected request credentials |
| UI | Navigation/translation/server adapters extracted without changing semantic tokens |
| Lettin | D1 session behavior, R2 permissions, schemas/data, draft/publication snapshots and writeAccess fences |
| Parley/Meet | Immutable scenarios, private facilitator reviews, participant invitations, signalling/media, Durable Objects and AI bindings |
| Runtime | SSR, assets, auth denial/redirects, cache, errors, cancellation and bindings in real local Workers with isolated fixtures |
| Delivery | Exact-commit CI build, staging runtime acceptance, then authorized canonical promotion with rollback and product checks |

Prove a small authenticated vertical slice before replacing the complete app.
Document fixture boundaries and hosted dependencies: local Durable Objects do not
validate Cloudflare SFU/TURN. Hosting adoption does not imply migrating every store
to D1 or replacing Supabase. Database changes, schedules, secrets and canonical
traffic each need a bounded plan. Pin the promotion range, retain a rollback
artifact and verify schema/binding compatibility and health before promotion.

## Runaway-work and cost acceptance

Every migration or change that adds or amplifies billable work must include a
cost-safety review. The [reported runaway Durable Object alarm incident](https://serverlesshorrors.com/all/cloudflare-108k/)
is a warning about self-sustaining work, not an independently verified account
of provider usage. Do not rely on future refunds, billing notifications or a
per-invocation CPU limit to cap total storage, requests, retries or downstream spend.

[Durable Object alarms](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/alarms/)
are at-least-once and automatically retry thrown errors. Explicit rescheduling can
create another chain beyond those retries. Ingress rate limits cannot stop work
that an alarm, queue consumer or cron trigger already owns.

| Control | Acceptance evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Work bounds | Bound operations, scanned rows/pages, payload size, fan-out and concurrency per wake; bound attempts and elapsed age for finite jobs. Persistent failures or no progress exhaust a durable budget rather than resetting on wake or restart. |
| Scheduling | Empty/completed/expired/cancelled jobs do not reschedule. A valid next deadline is finite and in the future; retries use capped backoff. Recurring activity requires an explicit owner and renewable lease/expiry, with a documented stop path. |
| Retry identity | Duplicate delivery and restarts preserve job identity, attempts, cursor and idempotency fences. A consumer cannot re-enter its own enqueue path indefinitely. Checkpoint progress without multiplying writes per item. |
| Durable shutdown | Check a persisted stop/lease fence before expensive work and before rescheduling, including racing callbacks. Test a scoped authenticated stop path that preserves resumable data. Removing public routes or stopping ingress is insufficient. |
| Storage amplification | Use indexed/bounded reads; avoid unbounded list/scan fallback in hot paths. Batch writes where useful, then measure the actual billing unit: batching does not necessarily reduce billed keys/rows/messages. |
| Cost envelope | Record normal and failure-case operation counts per job/session and expected maximum admitted concurrency/volume. Include storage, queue retries, AI/media and logging; calculate with current product pricing and record assumptions. |
| Detection and response | Verify which usage/anomaly alerts the account and products support, who receives them and how quickly they can react. Record sampled per-service rates, retry/no-progress counters and a tested independent operator stop procedure. |

Require regressions for empty queues, expired state, duplicate execution, restart,
clock/deadline boundaries, persistent downstream failure, no progress and stop-versus-
reschedule races. Count storage/downstream calls as well as final return values;
prove bounds under repeated wakes in isolated fixtures and the real local Worker.
Exact-commit CI must exercise the emitted artifact. Keep live account settings,
alert delivery and hosted shutdown verification as separate production evidence.

Meet class attendance erasure is bounded. A successful delete is one fence SQL
statement, one room post per room (two for a subject), one directory queue,
one directory forget, and one SQL delete. An unchanged subject list does not
write the directory. A failure stores one pending row, posts at most four
rooms at a time, and drains at most eight directory erasures per alarm. Each
directory attempt is durable: three failures stop that entry, and an index
publish retries three times, a minute apart, and then stops. The daily purge
finishes at most 50 confirmed pending rows. An empty erase queue does not
schedule another alarm. A repeated generation does not reset attempt counts.
A changed directory publish writes the room snapshot once more to clear its
retry deadline.

The daily attendance retention slot runs up to eight 200-row purge RPCs and one
erasure-intent RPC. An empty or short purge page ends the loop. The slot checks
the durable job fence before each call, and the SQL functions independently
honor the database stop fence. A deadline reserve leaves time for the intent
scan. Deletes are idempotent and the processor schedules no follow-up. The
`meet-attendance-retention.test.ts` dispatch cases count calls through a full
batch, deadline pressure and a stop between pages.

The daily `external-app-exchange-audit-retention` slot makes at most eight
1,000-row purge RPCs and ten ledger operations (claim, eight fence checks,
outcome), on an existing trigger. While the purge function is missing it makes
one call a day, uncharged only until 2026-12-07 23:59 GMT+7. Hosted stop and
billing evidence are still outstanding; see the
[processor runbook](/build/devops/cloudflare-processor-migration#native-maintenance-external-app-exchange-audit-retention).

Cron Control's default-off checkout Worker uses a 5,000-item combined active and
quarantine bound, pre-expiry capacity checks, three durable attempts per item,
per-workspace invalidation receipts and a 240-second whole-run deadline. Stop is
checked before each expiry batch and invalidation chunk. See the
[processor runbook](/build/devops/cloudflare-processor-migration) for counted
operation bounds, restart/deadline/poison regressions and remaining hosted stop
and cache-freshness evidence. Source and mocked requests do not establish billed
usage or crash-atomic database-to-ledger persistence.

Cron Control's default-off database history job adds one RPC per enabled ten-minute
slot, deleting at most 1,000 completed rows per table. It has no in-slot retry or
drain loop; the existing durable slot claim, pre-delete stop fence and five-failure
budget survive ledger restarts. Counted dispatch/stop regressions and full-chain
pgTAP cover the bounds and seven-day cutoff. The
history retention runbook
records the daily operation envelope and stop procedure. Hosted scheduled execution,
independent operator-stop acceptance and billed usage remain rollout evidence.

### Mastermind ship collector envelope

The `mastermind-ship` Cron Control job is default-off and adds no trigger: it
runs every second minute on the existing one-minute trigger, and dispatch
skips odd minutes before any ledger call. A run makes at most 32 provider reads (GitHub and the
Cloudflare API, neither billed per call), two Mastermind store requests and
about twelve ledger calls, with one attempt per slot and a 40-second
deadline. A conditional probe answered 304 skips the GitHub query; 403 and
429 back a source off for one minute to one hour. Check now shares the
ledger claim, so the last claimed slot limits it to one run per 30 seconds
and the lease refuses overlap. The durable job stop, the five-slot failure
budget (a slot with every configured source failing is `failed`) and the
store fence each end work before the next provider call.
At 720 slots a day the store sees 1,440 row writes (of its 50,000 daily
budget). `apps/cron-control/src/mastermind-ship.test.ts` counts provider and
store calls through stop, restart, backoff, failure and rate-limit cases. The
[runbook](../devops/mastermind-ship-collector.mdx) owns enablement and stop.
Hosted execution and billed usage remain rollout evidence.

### Mastermind Inbox push envelope

With dispatch off, signed fleet publishes do no extra reads or sends. An
enabled publish adds one previous-snapshot read. With eligible new cards,
dispatch checks one owner's permission, push preferences and devices. It
processes at most 50 cards in batches of eight within an eight-second
dispatch deadline. Each batch can claim each card once, read the snapshot and
answers at most twice each, and attempt the daily budget compare-and-set at
most three times. A full budget, exhausted contention or a store failure
stops dispatch. The durable budget admits at most 100 cards per UTC day
across restarts. Each admitted card can reach at most 10 devices, for a
ceiling of 1,000 FCM device submissions per day.

Dispatch schedules no work and never retries an uncertain FCM submission.
Restore the last serving version with dispatch off to stop new sends. The
`decision-push.test.ts` and fleet route tests cover repeated publishes,
provider failure, restart, owner scoping and disabled dispatch. Hosted
operation counts and the live stop procedure remain rollout evidence.
See the [delivery contract](/reference/api-reference/mastermind-push-events#fleet-inbox-cards).

### Fleet dry-run and retention envelope

Fleet reuses one existing 15-minute Cron Control trigger. Disabled mode
adds no network or ledger calls. One admitted run has a 90-second deadline
and performs one status read, one claim, at most 20 receipts and one purge.
Each Web request invokes one private Postgres RPC. The purge deletes at
most 1,000 rows per slot across the three retention stores and writes one
counts-only audit record. An empty queue still runs retention. A stopped
database costs at most the status request before mutations. An ambiguous
response ends the slot without retry. There are no provider, AI, queue,
alarm or lane calls.

At 96 slots per day, a full queue permits 2,208 Web requests and as many
Postgres RPCs, 1,920 examined intents, 96,000 retention deletes and 96
counts-only purge audit rows. Each slot has at most 25 ledger RPCs
(claim, fence per request, completion), 25 logical ledger reads, two
logical writes and one completion report with counts. This yields up to
2,400 ledger RPCs and 192 logical writes per day from admitted runs.
A duplicate tick checks the ledger once. The SQL slot watermark prevents
an extra claim batch or deletion on replay. Delivery duplicates and
external requests are outside the scheduled operation count.

At Cloudflare's paid overage rates, 72,000 ledger requests and 5,760 logical
ledger row writes over 30 days contribute approximately $0.017 combined
if both dimensions are fully overage and each write bills one row.
Compute, physical storage, logs and the Web/Postgres bill depend on
measured service usage and shared plan allowances.
[Cloudflare Workers pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/).

Tests count calls at full batch, exercise the Worker mode and persisted
ledger stop and restart after lost claim and receipt responses. SQL
regressions cover bounded deletes, replay, and stale approvals after a
database stop and resume. Hosted stop readback, emitted-Worker execution
and billed usage remain activation evidence. See the
[Fleet consumer runbook](/build/devops/overview#fleet-dry-run-consumer).

The Mastermind store Worker (`apps/mastermind-store`) has no alarms, crons,
queues or in-Worker retries. It caps ops per request, value size and live
rows, charges a durable daily write budget before running a batch, deletes at
most 20 expired rows per write, and holds a durable operator stop fence. Its
cost envelope and regressions are in the
[Mastermind store runbook](/build/devops/mastermind-store).
Its fleet bridge Durable Object holds hibernatable WebSockets with no alarms,
charges a durable daily operation budget, caps the outbox, tickets and reply
rates, and stops behind the same operator fence; see
[Fleet bridge](/build/devops/mastermind-store#fleet-bridge).

The deploy coordinator Worker (`apps/deploy-coordinator`) schedules nothing:
lease lapses and queue expiry are applied lazily at the start of each call. Its
objects are limited to catalog projects × three environments, each charging a
durable 500-call daily budget before other work and holding a durable
environment stop fence. Text-keyed tables are `WITHOUT ROWID`, and rows
written are counted with their index rows and pinned per call by a cost test:
at most 18 a create, 6 for any other call once deferred transitions are
charged to the create they belong to. Clients poll with backoff and heartbeat
every four minutes, so a worst-case deployment is about 36 calls. With every
environment at budget the hard ceiling is about $0.10 a month above the plan
standalone, about $31 a month marginal once other Workers use up the shared
included allowances; the figures and the stop order are in the
[deployment coordinator design](/build/devops/deployment-coordinator#cost-and-stop-fence-analysis).

The abuse-guard store Worker (`apps/abuse-guard`) keeps its bounded-work and
stop-fence evidence in the [abuse-guard store runbook](/build/devops/abuse-guard-store).
It carries a few accounting limits:
- Its daily budget counts admitted commands, not billed rows. One `win.hit` writes
  up to four window rows plus a dedupe record, and one `res.reserve` writes up to
  three rows plus a dedupe record.
- Replay/password command admission now checks durable source/principal quotas
  and charges family usage in one control-object transaction. Each identity gets
  at most 5% of the family share per UTC day. Denied subject commands and success
  refunds count; cache eviction/restart never resets the quota.
- Fair admission adds one control DO request per cache miss and up to two quota
  rows plus a control-state write on admission. Rejected probes do not spend
  subject commands, but their request billing remains unbounded without accepted
  ingress controls. The command budget is not a total dollar cap. Hosted request
  sizing and partition capacity remain activation holds.
- Other families reserve the entire batch in a durable control transaction before
  executing subjects. Each admitted batch adds a control request and a control-state
  row read/write. Interrupted and skipped work remains charged. The workerd
  restart-before-flush regression replaces the runtime between admissions and
  verifies that reservations survive and the family budget cannot be bypassed.
  Operator stops reject new admissions; request billing remains an activation hold.
- The theoretical storage ceiling is 2 KiB × 120-day retention × the daily budget.
  Only replay fences use long TTLs, and their values are tiny.

The [Playground execution runbook](/build/devops/playground-execution)
records the Cloudflare Run limits, restart and stop behavior, and container
billing assumptions. Hosted isolation and shutdown evidence precede activation.

CPU limits constrain an invocation, not the number of invocations or all billable
services. Usage notifications are detection, not an automatic spending cutoff.
Choose service-specific limits with measured workloads; do not silently apply an
arbitrary global value that breaks realtime or recovery behavior. See current
[Workers pricing and custom CPU limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/)
and [available billing alerts](https://developers.cloudflare.com/notifications/notification-available/).
Any automatic circuit breaker must itself perform bounded work and fail safely
without deleting original data or retrying indefinitely.

Existing tests and code must be inspected per service; this foundation establishes
review gates and does not assert that every deployed alarm is protected or that
account alerts are configured.

### Hive maintenance and native migration

The Hive maintenance module (`apps/hive/maintenance/worker.mjs`) returns one
fixed response per request with zero upstream calls, bindings, body reads or
background jobs. Focused tests cover HTTP methods, WebSocket rejection and zero
external work. Request volume can still incur charges. Hosted route removal and
script deletion are its durable stop procedure; that control-plane rehearsal is
pending separately approved staging access, not proven by source tests.
See the maintenance runbook.

The native migration plan requires
persisted budgets and generation/stop fences before simulation, queues, alarms
or model calls can be enabled. Operation-count, crash/restart and stop-versus-
reschedule evidence remains pending implementation. No Hive native scheduler or
paid storage/AI resource is enabled by this plan.

### Wave-1 staging publishers: publication and serving envelope

Calendar, Mail and Apps staging publishers require an exact owner-reviewed
source/artifact admission and authenticated D1 consumption state. PR GitHub tokens
cannot write that staging-account ledger; missing/deleted/invalid state fails closed.
Seven bounded D1 queries persist/read back three transitions on a fresh success;
there is one upload invocation, no application retry and no automatic admission
renewal. The real-entrypoint stop-fence negative control, forged/deleted-state
fixtures and SQLite conditional-update races live in `scripts/ci/wave1-native-*.test.js`.

Staging configs disable workers.dev and preview URLs and have no public routes,
including Meet's prepared profiles. This removes public request amplification;
rate limits, CPU caps and the publication flag alone would not cap serving costs.
The owner must verify hosted topology before enablement. Disable publication and
delete/disable only the staging Worker to stop unexpected execution, preserving
consumption evidence. The publisher runbook
owns provisioning, HMAC/token rotation, finite counts and the stop procedure.
Hosted credential scope, private runtime acceptance and actual serving state remain
separate release evidence. Production publication stays held for all four apps.

### Turbo remote cache: R2 operation envelope

`apps/turbo-cache` ships with `TURBO_CACHE_MODE=off`, which performs no R2
or DO operations on artifact paths. `budget-v2` in the global Durable Object is
the authoritative fence/counters. Every reservation and admin mutation uses a
storage transaction, committed before allowance. Missing/corrupt/unavailable
state fails closed. Denials and repeated unchanged admin actions do not write;
unknown reservation outcomes are denied without retry or refund. Native DO
storage/output gates preserve charges and fences across restart.

There are **zero R2 control writes**, including initialization, admin actions and
bursts. `_control/budget-v1` is read only on explicit first initialization to
import prior usage; it is never an admission source or live checkpoint. Delayed
legacy writes cannot overwrite migrated DO state. Disable/drain the old revision
and reconcile unresolved writes before import. No periodic job, alarm or retry
loop exists; each request has at most one admission transaction.

The maximum batch is 50 hashes × four scopes (200 HEADs). Including DO and
rate-limit calls, its conservative operation count is 202 under the configured
208 ceiling. `apps/turbo-cache/src/stop-regression.test.ts` and
`budget-integrity.test.ts` cover counts, failed/unknown transactions, concurrent
reservations, delayed legacy completion after stop and restart, a 600-request
burst with simulated control-write 429s, migration and coalesced admin actions.
The workerd script verifies actual transactional initialization and fence/restart.
Exact-commit build/runtime CI remains required. DO requests/storage and denied
or status ingress remain traffic-dependent costs outside R2 admission counters;
there is no fixed total-spend guarantee. Set mode off to stop artifact storage/DO
calls or disable the Worker route to stop invocations. The
[runbook](../devops/turbo-remote-cache.mdx) owns migration, pricing review and stop.

## Incident evidence

Correlate scoped failing requests with authenticated Worker tail exceptions and
the deployed revision. A hung-request cancellation establishes a runtime failure;
nearby framework warnings are clues, not root-cause proof. Offline artifact replay
can isolate middleware/server boundaries, but missing modules or post-build config
patches do not establish a valid replacement release. Keep raw logs private.
Build success alone does not establish request health.

Follow [active runtime ownership](/build/devops/active-runtime) and the
[delivery runbook](/build/devops/github-actions-runbook). Release builds remain in
CI; a migration direction does not authorize production cutover.

### Meet saved whiteboard cost bounds

The Meet realtime Worker declares `WhiteboardRoomDurableObject` (SQLite,
migration `v4-whiteboard`), one object per meeting and board. Its alarm is the
only scheduler and every wake is derived from durable state, so a quiet board
schedules nothing.

Per board, per participant message the room does no storage or network work.
Under continuous editing it writes storage at most once per 5 seconds and calls
the platform at most once per 15 seconds, each flush guarded by a persisted
three-attempt, two-minute budget that survives restarts. A connected room adds
one 60-second expiry sweep. The last disconnect schedules one flush and stops.
The scene is bounded at 2000 elements and 2,000,000 bytes and stored in
256 KB chunks, so a full board costs at most about nine storage rows per persist.
The platform route does two database reads and one compare-and-set write per
flush. `MEET_WHITEBOARD_FLUSH_DISABLED` (`true` or `1`) halts storage writes and
flushes at every wake; the room then relays live traffic only.

`packages/realtime/src/meet/board-sync-core.test.ts` counts storage writes, alarm
sets and flushes for a 500-edit burst and ten minutes of continuous edits, and
covers the fence, an outage that exhausts the budget, a persistent failure
followed by a later edit, restart after unfinished work and a conflict.
`apps/meet-realtime/src/whiteboard-room-do.test.ts` runs the Durable Object
adapter against the fence. Hosted alarm behavior, account ingress budgets and
the operator stop rehearsal remain activation evidence.

### Fleet Board coordination cost bounds

The Ops Hub Fleet Board source declares a SQLite Durable Object and a follow-up
Queue. Each board starts stopped. Its control row holds the stop generation and
hourly admission counters. The stop action advances the generation. Stale Queue
envelopes cannot start work, and persisted retry state uses at most three
attempts. Operators can inspect the fence with `GET /board/control/stop` and
change it with a fresh manager assertion and a matching generation.

Per board and fixed UTC hour, the source allows up to 120 Tasks reads, 60 Queue
sends and 120 alarm writes. Claims read at most four candidate pages and check
user access to the selected task before committing a lease. Watcher fan-out
allows up to eight deliveries per event. Outbound notification adapters remain
unavailable until the recipient audience can be verified. SQLite tests cover
stopped dispatch, stale generations and lease expiry. Hosted Queue and alarm
behavior, account-level ingress budgets and the operator stop rehearsal remain
activation evidence.

Dispatch checks the agent's live delegation and Tasks eligibility before
verification. Message reads cache positive task access per user and task for
at most 60 seconds and recheck the channel grant after the Tasks response.
Stale completions may record the outcome of work already started. They do
not create watcher work. Set `BOARD_ASSERTION_AUDIENCE` to the same
environment and Worker origin identifier used by the gateway signer.

The board admits up to 200 live replay rows per actor for ordinary writes
and up to 250 for cleanup. Each actor may renew leases or cancel follow-ups
30 times per hour and create 15 watchers per hour. The board allows 256
enabled watchers, up to 16 per actor.
